Every number quoted in the Figure 3 results paragraph is computed here, from the
same artifacts the figure itself is drawn from. Nothing in the prose should be
typed by hand — if a number changes, re-knit this and update the text.

**Scope:** Figure 3 only. This is deliberately separate from the hero-number
document.

**The slice matters.** `Vis_Code/combined_realdata_figure.R` builds panels A and
C from a specific subset: **maternal panel**, **Adjusted** model, **log1p**
scale, non-asthma outcomes. (Opening it to both panels was tried on 2026-08-11
and reverted -- see the comment in the `results-slice` chunk.) (Until 2026-08-10 it also excluded CCREOH; that filter was
undocumented, CCREOH proved not to be an outlier, and it has been removed from
all four scripts that carried it.) Panel B is read from
`cohort_regime_diagnostic.R` output, restricted to `panel == "mat"` (via the
`semi_join` onto panel A's pair list, which carries `panel`) and it uses the
**Unadjusted**
decomposition on purpose (Study is the confounder under study; adjusting would
drop cohorts on covariate completeness).

So the panel-B class percentages are **not** the same as the headline numbers in
`cohort_regime_summary.csv`, which cover both panels and all pairs. Both are
reported below, clearly labelled. Quote the panel-B ones when describing
Figure 3.

## The panel A / C slice, reproduced exactly

```{r results-slice}
result_paths <- list.files(exwas_root, pattern = "exposure_results_table\\.parquet$",
                           recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
# Guard: only the current output layout. A legacy layout without scale= once
# coexisted here and was double-counted by the figure scripts.
result_paths <- result_paths[grepl("scale=", result_paths)]
NUM$n_result_files <- length(result_paths)

results <- bind_rows(lapply(result_paths, read_parquet)) %>%
  # Mirrors combined_realdata_figure.R. The `!study %in% c("CCREOH")` filter that
  # used to sit here was removed 2026-08-10 in both files -- it was undocumented
  # and CCREOH is not an outlier in this slice.
  # MATERNAL ONLY (reverted 2026-08-11 at the author's request). Opening the
  # figure to both panels was tried and rolled back: it took panel A from 44 to
  # 61 rows and weakened every headline (discordance excess over the permutation
  # null +5.4pp -> +3.4pp, panel C rho 0.11 -> 0.03) while mixing maternal and
  # child estimates of the same analyte, which are different
  # exposure-outcome relationships. The child-only cardiometabolic outcomes
  # (GOALS, NASH, SEARCH, CHARGE, MDUC) are therefore out of this figure again.
  # `panel` is still carried through the joins below -- with one panel it is
  # constant, but the keys stay correct if the filter is ever lifted.
  filter(status == "ok", model == "Adjusted", panel == "mat",
         !outcome %in% c("Asthma", "Severe_Asthma"),
         !is.na(beta)) %>%
  mutate(
    # SE (2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 3.8). The ExWAS now
    # records `se` directly, so use it when present. The /3.92 reconstruction is
    # kept only as a fallback for result trees written before that change: it
    # assumes a 1.96 critical value, but the linear CIs use qt(0.975, n-p), so it
    # overestimates se by ~6% at df = 20 and biases every rma() fit below.
    se = if ("se" %in% names(.)) {
      coalesce(se, case_when(
        outcome_type == "continuous" ~ (ci_high - ci_low) / 3.92,
        TRUE ~ (log(pmax(ci_high, 1e-9)) - log(pmax(ci_low, 1e-9))) / 3.92))
    } else {
      case_when(
        outcome_type == "continuous" ~ (ci_high - ci_low) / 3.92,
        TRUE ~ (log(pmax(ci_high, 1e-9)) - log(pmax(ci_low, 1e-9))) / 3.92)
    },
    outcome_clean = case_when(
      outcome == "Gest_Age_Birth" ~ "Gestational Age",
      outcome == "Preterm_Birth"  ~ "Preterm Birth",
      TRUE ~ outcome)
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(beta), is.finite(se), se > 0)

strip_df <- results %>%
  filter(scale == "log1p") %>%
  mutate(z = beta / se, pair = paste0(exposure, " | ", outcome_clean)) %>%
  group_by(pair) %>% filter(n_distinct(study) >= 2) %>%
  mutate(discordant = any(z > 0) & any(z < 0)) %>% ungroup()

NUM$panelA_pairs    <- n_distinct(strip_df$pair)
NUM$panelA_cohorts  <- n_distinct(strip_df$study)
NUM$panelA_outcomes <- n_distinct(strip_df$outcome_clean)
NUM$panelA_exposures<- n_distinct(strip_df$exposure)
NUM$panelA_estimates<- nrow(strip_df)
NUM$discord_pct     <- 100 * mean(distinct(strip_df, pair, discordant)$discordant)
NUM$panelA_z_min    <- min(strip_df$z); NUM$panelA_z_max <- max(strip_df$z)
NUM$panelA_sig_pct  <- 100 * mean(strip_df$p_value < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

# How many pairs have at least one cohort significant in EACH direction --
# the strongest form of visible disagreement.
NUM$panelA_sig_both_dir <- strip_df %>%
  group_by(pair) %>%
  summarise(both = any(z > 0 & p_value < 0.05) & any(z < 0 & p_value < 0.05),
            .groups = "drop") %>% pull(both) %>% sum()

tibble(metric = names(NUM), value = unlist(NUM)) %>% knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r panelA-discordance-null}
# NULL BENCHMARK FOR DISCORDANCE (added 2026-08-11, audit section 1.6).
#
# `discordant` = the pair contains both a positive and a negative z, with no
# precision condition. Under a true null the sign of each cohort's z is a coin
# flip, so a pair with K cohorts is discordant with probability 1 - 2^(1-K):
# 50% at K=2, 75% at K=3. Most of this panel sits at K=2. The observed rate is
# therefore only evidence of real cross-cohort disagreement to the extent it
# exceeds that baseline -- quote the EXCESS, not the raw percentage.
#
# Two baselines are reported:
#   analytic  - 1 - 2^(1-K), exact under independent coin-flip signs
#   permuted  - sign(z) shuffled within each pair, which additionally respects
#               the observed imbalance between positive and negative estimates
k_by_pair <- strip_df %>% group_by(pair) %>% summarise(K = n_distinct(study), .groups = "drop")
NUM$discord_null_analytic <- 100 * mean(1 - 2^(1 - k_by_pair$K))

set.seed(20260811)
# 500 permutations of the whole panel (not per-pair), so the null RATE is already
# an average over all pairs -- its Monte Carlo SE here is ~0.5pp, ample for the
# comparison being made. Reduced from 2000 for rerun turnaround (2026-08-11).
n_perm <- 500
signs <- sign(strip_df$z)
pair_id <- strip_df$pair
perm_rates <- replicate(n_perm, {
  shuffled <- sample(signs)
  tapply(shuffled, pair_id, function(s) any(s > 0) && any(s < 0)) |> mean()
})
NUM$discord_null_permuted <- 100 * mean(perm_rates)
NUM$discord_null_perm_lo  <- 100 * quantile(perm_rates, 0.025)
NUM$discord_null_perm_hi  <- 100 * quantile(perm_rates, 0.975)
NUM$discord_excess        <- NUM$discord_pct - NUM$discord_null_permuted
NUM$discord_perm_p        <- mean(perm_rates >= NUM$discord_pct / 100)

tibble(
  metric = c("observed discordance %", "null (analytic, 1-2^(1-K)) %",
             "null (permuted signs) %", "null 95% interval",
             "EXCESS over null (pp)", "permutation p"),
  value = c(round(NUM$discord_pct, 1), round(NUM$discord_null_analytic, 1),
            round(NUM$discord_null_permuted, 1),
            sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", NUM$discord_null_perm_lo, NUM$discord_null_perm_hi),
            round(NUM$discord_excess, 1), signif(NUM$discord_perm_p, 3))
) %>% knitr::kable()

cat("\nPairs by K (discordance is near-automatic at small K):\n")
k_by_pair %>% count(K, name = "pairs") %>%
  mutate(null_discordant_pct = round(100 * (1 - 2^(1 - K)), 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r panelA-composition}
# Which outcomes, exposures and cohorts the panel actually spans -- needed so the
# text can describe the figure's scope without guessing.
NUM$panelA_outcome_list <- paste(sort(unique(strip_df$outcome_clean)), collapse = ", ")
NUM$panelA_cohort_list  <- paste(sort(unique(strip_df$study)), collapse = ", ")

# Panel A colours by cohort LOCATION, which lives in Harmonized_SDOH, not in the
# ExWAS output -- so join it the same way combined_realdata_figure.R does
# (modal Location per study) rather than assuming one location per cohort.
load("../../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Harmonized_SDOH.RData")
study_loc <- SDOH_Data_All %>%
  # std_study() for consistency with every other cohort key (2026-08-11).
  mutate(study = std_study(Study),
         Location = as.character(Location)) %>%
  count(study, Location, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(study) %>% slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% ungroup() %>%
  select(study, location = Location)

NUM$panelA_location_n <- strip_df %>% distinct(study) %>%
  left_join(study_loc, by = "study") %>% pull(location) %>% n_distinct()
NUM$panelA_location_list <- strip_df %>% distinct(study) %>%
  left_join(study_loc, by = "study") %>% pull(location) %>% unique() %>% sort() %>%
  paste(collapse = ", ")
strip_df %>% count(outcome_clean, name = "estimates") %>%
  left_join(strip_df %>% distinct(panel, outcome_clean, pair) %>% count(outcome_clean, name = "pairs"),
            by = "outcome_clean") %>% knitr::kable()
cat("cohorts:", NUM$panelA_cohort_list, "\n")
cat("outcomes:", NUM$panelA_outcome_list, "\n")
```

# Per-pair spread in z, to characterise "how far apart" cohorts land.
spread_tbl <- strip_df %>% group_by(pair) %>%
  summarise(k = n_distinct(study), z_range = max(z) - min(z), .groups = "drop")
NUM$panelA_median_z_range <- median(spread_tbl$z_range)
NUM$panelA_max_z_range    <- max(spread_tbl$z_range)
NUM$panelA_k2_pairs       <- sum(spread_tbl$k == 2)

## Panel B — the decomposition actually displayed

```{r panelB}
A_pairs <- results %>% filter(scale == "log1p") %>%
  group_by(panel, outcome, exposure) %>% filter(n_distinct(study) >= 2) %>%
  ungroup() %>% distinct(panel, outcome, exposure)

decomp <- read_csv(file.path(diag_dir, "cohort_regime_pairs.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  semi_join(A_pairs, by = c("panel", "outcome", "analyte" = "exposure"))

NUM$panelB_pairs <- nrow(decomp)

panelB_class <- decomp %>% count(class) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>% arrange(desc(n))
panelB_class %>% knitr::kable(digits = 1)

get_pct <- function(cl) {
  x <- panelB_class$pct[panelB_class$class == cl]; if (length(x)) x else 0
}
get_n <- function(cl) {
  x <- panelB_class$n[panelB_class$class == cl]; if (length(x)) x else 0
}
NUM$panelB_n_concordant   <- get_n("concordant")
NUM$panelB_n_magnitude    <- get_n("magnitude_distort")
NUM$panelB_n_reversal     <- get_n("sign_reversal")
NUM$panelB_pct_concordant <- get_pct("concordant")
NUM$panelB_pct_magnitude  <- get_pct("magnitude_distort")
NUM$panelB_pct_reversal   <- get_pct("sign_reversal")
NUM$panelB_n_strong_rev   <- sum(decomp$strong_reversal, na.rm = TRUE)
NUM$panelB_pct_between_opposes <- 100 * mean(decomp$between_opposes_within, na.rm = TRUE)

# How much pooling moves the estimate, on the partial-correlation scale.
NUM$panelB_median_shift <- median(abs(decomp$r_naive - decomp$r_within), na.rm = TRUE)
NUM$panelB_max_shift    <- max(abs(decomp$r_naive - decomp$r_within), na.rm = TRUE)
# Naive pooling inflates |effect| relative to the within-cohort estimate?
NUM$panelB_pct_inflated <- 100 * mean(abs(decomp$r_naive) > abs(decomp$r_within), na.rm = TRUE)

decomp %>%
  transmute(pair = paste0(analyte, " | ", outcome), K, class,
            r_within = round(r_within, 3), r_naive = round(r_naive, 3),
            r_between = round(r_between, 3), I2 = round(I2, 1)) %>%
  arrange(class, pair) %>% knitr::kable()
```

## Does the sign-reversal rate survive the creatinine-correction artifact?

Four of the 13 cohorts are dilution-corrected in `HHEAR_Data_Clean_Targeted_V3.Rmd`
(`cre_correct()` divides concentration by urinary creatinine); nine are not.
Naive pooling pools `log1p(concentration)` across cohorts, so a pair that mixes
corrected and uncorrected cohorts is pooling values on two different scales — and
that alone can manufacture a within-vs-pooled discrepancy. This chunk asks whether
the reversal rate holds inside pairs whose cohorts all share a correction status.

Labels were established two independent ways, which agree: (1) the presence of a
`cre_correct()` call in each cohort's block, and (2) an empirical comparison of
harmonised against raw source concentrations — the corrected cohorts show a median
harmonised/raw ratio of 0.006–0.018 *with per-person spread* (a divisor), the rest
sit at 1.0. NHBCS's empirical check was inconclusive (its raw table carries both
`Mother_pid` and `child_pid`, so the join is unreliable) but it has no
`cre_correct()` call and its medians sit with the uncorrected cohorts.

```{r correction-strata}
CRE_CORRECTED <- c("DCHS", "SWSD", "THS", "ZIP")

pair_status <- results %>% filter(scale == "log1p") %>%
  group_by(panel, outcome, exposure) %>%
  summarise(k = n_distinct(study),
            n_corr = n_distinct(study[study %in% CRE_CORRECTED]),
            n_raw  = n_distinct(study[!study %in% CRE_CORRECTED]),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(k >= 2) %>%
  mutate(stratum = case_when(n_corr > 0 & n_raw == 0 ~ "all corrected",
                             n_raw  > 0 & n_corr == 0 ~ "all uncorrected",
                             TRUE ~ "mixed"))

decomp_strat <- decomp %>%
  inner_join(pair_status, by = c("panel", "outcome", "analyte" = "exposure"))

stopifnot(nrow(decomp_strat) == nrow(decomp))   # no pair lost in the join

by_stratum <- decomp_strat %>%
  group_by(stratum) %>%
  summarise(pairs = n(),
            reversal = sum(class == "sign_reversal"),
            magnitude = sum(class == "magnitude_distort"),
            concordant = sum(class == "concordant"),
            pct_reversal = 100 * mean(class == "sign_reversal"),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(pairs))
by_stratum %>% knitr::kable(digits = 1)

NUM$strat_mixed_pairs      <- by_stratum$pairs[by_stratum$stratum == "mixed"]
NUM$strat_uncorr_pairs     <- by_stratum$pairs[by_stratum$stratum == "all uncorrected"]
NUM$strat_uncorr_reversal  <- by_stratum$reversal[by_stratum$stratum == "all uncorrected"]
NUM$strat_uncorr_pct       <- by_stratum$pct_reversal[by_stratum$stratum == "all uncorrected"]
NUM$strat_mixed_reversal   <- by_stratum$reversal[by_stratum$stratum == "mixed"]
NUM$strat_mixed_pct        <- by_stratum$pct_reversal[by_stratum$stratum == "mixed"]
if (any(by_stratum$stratum == "all corrected")) {
  NUM$strat_corr_pairs    <- by_stratum$pairs[by_stratum$stratum == "all corrected"]
  NUM$strat_corr_reversal <- by_stratum$reversal[by_stratum$stratum == "all corrected"]
  NUM$strat_corr_pct      <- by_stratum$pct_reversal[by_stratum$stratum == "all corrected"]
}
```

```{r correction-strata-panelA}
# Same question for panel A: is the direction discordance also inflated by pairs
# that mix correction statuses? Discordance is a per-pair property (does the pair
# contain both a positive and a negative z), so join the strata onto it.
discord_by_pair <- strip_df %>%
  group_by(panel, outcome, exposure) %>%
  summarise(discordant = any(z > 0) & any(z < 0), .groups = "drop")

discord_strat <- discord_by_pair %>% inner_join(pair_status, by = c("panel", "outcome", "exposure"))
stopifnot(nrow(discord_strat) == nrow(discord_by_pair))

by_stratum_A <- discord_strat %>%
  group_by(stratum) %>%
  # NOTE: n_discordant must not be named `discordant`. summarise() evaluates
  # sequentially, so a column named `discordant` would shadow the logical vector
  # and `mean()` would then average the COUNT, yielding percentages like 1400%.
  summarise(pairs = n(),
            n_discordant = sum(discordant),
            pct = 100 * mean(discordant), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(pairs))
stopifnot(all(by_stratum_A$pct >= 0 & by_stratum_A$pct <= 100),
          sum(by_stratum_A$n_discordant) == sum(discord_strat$discordant))
by_stratum_A %>% knitr::kable(digits = 1)

gA <- function(s, col) { v <- by_stratum_A[[col]][by_stratum_A$stratum == s]; if (length(v)) v else NA }
NUM$discA_uncorr_pairs <- gA("all uncorrected", "pairs")
NUM$discA_uncorr_n     <- gA("all uncorrected", "n_discordant")
NUM$discA_uncorr_pct   <- gA("all uncorrected", "pct")
NUM$discA_corr_pairs   <- gA("all corrected", "pairs")
NUM$discA_corr_n       <- gA("all corrected", "n_discordant")
NUM$discA_corr_pct     <- gA("all corrected", "pct")
NUM$discA_mixed_pairs  <- gA("mixed", "pairs")
NUM$discA_mixed_n      <- gA("mixed", "n_discordant")
NUM$discA_mixed_pct    <- gA("mixed", "pct")

tabA <- with(discord_strat, table(mixed = stratum == "mixed", discordant = discordant))
print(tabA)
if (all(dim(tabA) == c(2, 2))) {
  ftA <- fisher.test(tabA)
  NUM$discA_fisher_p  <- ftA$p.value
  NUM$discA_fisher_or <- unname(ftA$estimate)
  print(ftA)
}
```

```{r correction-strata-test}
# Is reversal associated with mixing correction status? Counts are small, so this
# is Fisher's exact on mixed vs same-status, reported as a descriptive check.
tab <- with(decomp_strat,
            table(mixed = stratum == "mixed", reversal = class == "sign_reversal"))
print(tab)
if (all(dim(tab) == c(2, 2))) {
  ft <- fisher.test(tab)
  NUM$strat_fisher_p  <- ft$p.value
  NUM$strat_fisher_or <- unname(ft$estimate)
  print(ft)
}
```

## How many cohorts each pair rests on, and what that does to the ecological slope

The `class` label compares `r_naive` against `r_within` and never uses
`r_between`, so the reversal classification itself is not affected by what
follows. But `r_between` is the *explanation* the figure offers — pooling pulls
the estimate toward the ecological relationship — and it is a correlation across
K cohort means. At K = 2 a correlation between two points is ±1 by construction,
carrying only a sign and no magnitude. These numbers support the limitation
paragraph in `Figure3_Results_Section.md`.

```{r ecological-degeneracy}
by_K <- decomp_strat %>%
  group_by(K) %>%
  summarise(pairs = n(),
            min_abs_between = min(abs(r_between)),
            med_abs_between = median(abs(r_between)),
            max_abs_between = max(abs(r_between)),
            all_exactly_one = all(abs(abs(r_between) - 1) < 1e-9),
            reversals = sum(class == "sign_reversal"),
            pct_reversal = 100 * mean(class == "sign_reversal"),
            .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(K)
by_K %>% knitr::kable(digits = 3)

NUM$K2_pairs            <- by_K$pairs[by_K$K == 2]
NUM$K2_pct_of_all       <- 100 * by_K$pairs[by_K$K == 2] / nrow(decomp_strat)
NUM$K2_between_all_one  <- by_K$all_exactly_one[by_K$K == 2]
NUM$K2_reversals        <- by_K$reversals[by_K$K == 2]
NUM$K2_pct_reversal     <- by_K$pct_reversal[by_K$K == 2]
NUM$Kge4_pairs          <- sum(decomp_strat$K >= 4)
NUM$Kge4_reversals      <- sum(decomp_strat$K >= 4 & decomp_strat$class == "sign_reversal")
NUM$Kge3_reversals      <- sum(decomp_strat$K >= 3 & decomp_strat$class == "sign_reversal")
NUM$Kle3_reversals      <- sum(decomp_strat$K <= 3 & decomp_strat$class == "sign_reversal")
NUM$Kge4_max_abs_between<- max(abs(decomp_strat$r_between[decomp_strat$K >= 4]))
NUM$max_K               <- max(decomp_strat$K)

# Every reversal in the figure comes from a pair with K <= 3 -- assert it so the
# limitation text cannot silently go stale.
stopifnot(NUM$Kle3_reversals == sum(decomp_strat$class == "sign_reversal"))

tibble(metric = grep("^K", names(NUM), value = TRUE),
       value = vapply(NUM[grep("^K", names(NUM))],
                      function(x) format(x, digits = 4), character(1))) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

## Panel C — heterogeneity vs concentration divergence

```{r panelC}
run_meta <- function(df) {
  fit <- tryCatch(rma(yi = df$beta, sei = df$se, method = "REML"),
                  error = function(e) tryCatch(rma(yi = df$beta, sei = df$se, method = "DL"),
                                               error = function(e) NULL))
  if (is.null(fit)) return(tibble())
  tibble(k = fit$k, I2 = fit$I2, tau2 = fit$tau2, QE = fit$QE, QEp = fit$QEp,
         pooled = as.numeric(fit$beta))
}

het_tbl <- results %>% filter(scale == "log1p") %>%
  group_by(panel, outcome_clean, exposure) %>% filter(n_distinct(study) >= 2) %>%
  group_modify(~ run_meta(.x)) %>% ungroup()

targeted <- read_csv(file.path(input_dir, "Harmonized_Targeted.csv"),
                     show_col_types = FALSE, locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"))

# PANEL C UNIT CONFOUND -- NOT FIXED (reverted 2026-08-11 at the author's request).
#
# `conc` is read straight off the Concentration column with NO unit conversion,
# then compared ACROSS cohorts as a max/min fold-change. 51 of 321 analytes are
# measured in more than one unit across cohorts, so this "concentration
# divergence" axis is substantially a unit artifact:
#
#     CRP  mg/L vs pg/mL  -> 308,146x   apparent fold-change, entirely units
#     Ba   ng/g vs ng/mL  ->      71x
#     Al   ng/g vs ng/ml  ->      36x
#
# See CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 1.2. The cohort-key fix below is retained
# (it is unrelated to units).
# Keyed by panel as well as study/exposure (2026-08-11), matching
# combined_realdata_figure.R: the median concentration of an analyte differs
# between mothers and children, so collapsing them blends two distributions.
conc_sum <- bind_rows(
    targeted %>% filter(!is.na(Mat_PID),   Mat_PID   != "") %>% mutate(panel = "mat"),
    targeted %>% filter(!is.na(Child_PID), Child_PID != "") %>% mutate(panel = "child")
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    panel,
    # std_study(), not str_remove("_Targeted$"): the latter yielded "NHBCS_Cot"
    # while the ExWAS results key on "NHBCS", so that cohort silently failed to
    # join and was dropped from the fold-change (audit section 3.5).
    study = std_study(Study),
    exposure = as.character(Analyte_Code),
    conc = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Concentration))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(conc), is.finite(conc), conc >= 0) %>%
  group_by(panel, study, exposure) %>%
  summarise(med = median(conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

div_tbl <- results %>% filter(scale == "log1p") %>%
  distinct(panel, outcome_clean, exposure, study) %>%
  left_join(conc_sum, by = c("panel", "study", "exposure")) %>%
  group_by(panel, outcome_clean, exposure) %>%
  summarise(med_fold = max(med, na.rm = TRUE) / pmax(min(med, na.rm = TRUE), 1e-9),
            .groups = "drop") %>% filter(is.finite(med_fold))

het_div <- het_tbl %>%
  left_join(div_tbl, by = c("panel", "outcome_clean", "exposure")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(med_fold))
stopifnot(nrow(het_div) <= nrow(het_tbl))

sp <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(log(het_div$med_fold), het_div$I2, method = "spearman"))
NUM$panelC_pairs      <- nrow(het_div)
NUM$panelC_rho        <- unname(sp$estimate)
NUM$panelC_p          <- sp$p.value
NUM$panelC_trend_drawn<- sp$p.value < 0.05
NUM$panelC_k2         <- sum(het_div$k == 2, na.rm = TRUE)
NUM$panelC_k2_pct     <- 100 * mean(het_div$k == 2, na.rm = TRUE)
NUM$panelC_I2_median  <- median(het_div$I2, na.rm = TRUE)
NUM$panelC_I2_over50  <- 100 * mean(het_div$I2 > 50, na.rm = TRUE)
NUM$panelC_fold_min   <- min(het_div$med_fold); NUM$panelC_fold_max <- max(het_div$med_fold)
NUM$panelC_I2_max     <- max(het_div$I2, na.rm = TRUE)

het_div %>% arrange(desc(I2)) %>%
  transmute(pair = paste0(exposure, " | ", outcome_clean), k,
            I2 = round(I2, 1), fold = round(med_fold, 1)) %>%
  head(10) %>% knitr::kable()
```

## Panel D (from 2026-08-10) — between-cohort exposure variance vs pooling distortion

Read from `panelD_variance_share.csv`, which `combined_realdata_figure.R` writes
when it builds the panel, so these numbers cannot drift from the plotted points.

```{r panelD-varshare}
vs <- read_csv(file.path(diag_dir, "panelD_variance_share.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  # `class` in this CSV carries the figure's DISPLAY labels ("Sign reversal
  # (Simpson)"), not the raw regime codes, because combined_realdata_figure.R
  # recodes them before writing. Match on the label, not on "sign_reversal".
  mutate(is_rev = grepl("Sign reversal", class))
stopifnot(any(vs$is_rev), !all(vs$is_rev))
NUM$pD_pairs        <- nrow(vs)
NUM$pD_icc_median   <- median(vs$icc)
NUM$pD_icc_min      <- min(vs$icc); NUM$pD_icc_max <- max(vs$icc)
NUM$pD_shift_max    <- max(vs$shift)

# `stratum` is now BIOLOGICAL MATRIX concordance (the panel's colour key since
# 2026-08-10); `cre_stratum` retains the creatinine grouping for the harmonisation
# paragraph, which still quotes it.
s_all   <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(vs$icc, vs$shift, method = "spearman"))
vs_same <- vs %>% filter(stratum == "Same matrix")
s_same  <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(vs_same$icc, vs_same$shift, method = "spearman"))
vs_diff <- vs %>% filter(stratum == "Different matrices")
s_diff  <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(vs_diff$icc, vs_diff$shift, method = "spearman"))

NUM$pD_rho_all  <- unname(s_all$estimate);  NUM$pD_p_all  <- s_all$p.value
NUM$pD_rho_same <- unname(s_same$estimate); NUM$pD_p_same <- s_same$p.value
NUM$pD_n_same   <- nrow(vs_same)
NUM$pD_rho_diff <- unname(s_diff$estimate); NUM$pD_p_diff <- s_diff$p.value
NUM$pD_n_diff   <- nrow(vs_diff)

by_strat_D <- vs %>% group_by(stratum) %>%
  summarise(pairs = n(), median_icc = median(icc), median_shift = median(shift),
            pct_reversal = 100 * mean(is_rev), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(pairs))
by_strat_D %>% knitr::kable(digits = 3)
vs %>% count(matrices, stratum) %>% knitr::kable()

gD <- function(s, col) { v <- by_strat_D[[col]][by_strat_D$stratum == s]; if (length(v)) v else NA }
NUM$pD_icc_same    <- gD("Same matrix", "median_icc")
NUM$pD_shift_same  <- gD("Same matrix", "median_shift")
NUM$pD_rev_same    <- gD("Same matrix", "pct_reversal")
NUM$pD_icc_diff    <- gD("Different matrices", "median_icc")
NUM$pD_shift_diff  <- gD("Different matrices", "median_shift")
NUM$pD_rev_diff    <- gD("Different matrices", "pct_reversal")
NUM$pD_shift_ratio <- NUM$pD_shift_diff / NUM$pD_shift_same
NUM$pD_n_blood_urine <- sum(vs$matrices == "Blood + Urine")
NUM$pD_n_blood_other <- sum(vs$matrices == "Blood + Other")
NUM$pD_wilcox_shift_matrix <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(shift ~ stratum, data = vs))$p.value
NUM$pD_wilcox_icc_matrix   <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(icc ~ stratum, data = vs))$p.value

# Creatinine grouping retained for the harmonisation paragraph.
by_cre_D <- vs %>% group_by(cre_stratum) %>%
  summarise(pairs = n(), median_icc = median(icc), median_shift = median(shift),
            .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(desc(pairs))
by_cre_D %>% knitr::kable(digits = 3)
gC <- function(s, col) { v <- by_cre_D[[col]][by_cre_D$cre_stratum == s]; if (length(v)) v else NA }
NUM$pD_icc_corr   <- gC("All creatinine-corrected", "median_icc")
NUM$pD_shift_corr <- gC("All creatinine-corrected", "median_shift")
NUM$pD_icc_unc    <- gC("All uncorrected", "median_icc")
NUM$pD_shift_unc  <- gC("All uncorrected", "median_shift")
NUM$pD_icc_mixed  <- gC("Mixed correction status", "median_icc")

# ICC predicts the SHIFT robustly but not the binary reversal label once mixing
# is controlled -- recorded so the text does not overclaim.
NUM$pD_wilcox_all  <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(icc ~ is_rev, data = vs))$p.value
NUM$pD_wilcox_same <- suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(icc ~ is_rev, data = vs_same))$p.value

tibble(metric = grep("^pD_", names(NUM), value = TRUE),
       value = vapply(NUM[grep("^pD_", names(NUM))],
                      function(x) format(x, digits = 3), character(1))) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

## Supplementary — the budget-allocation cost curve (was panel D until 2026-08-10)

Now `Final_Patchplots/Supp_Pooling_Budget_Tradeoff.pdf`. Numbers retained here
because the Discussion still refers to the trade-off.

```{r panelD}
budget <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "Pooling_Sim_Output",
                             "budget_allocation_results.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
names(budget)
# Crossover = where the "many diverse cohorts" and "one deep cohort" curves meet.
NUM$panelD_rows <- nrow(budget)
budget %>% knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

```{r panelD-crossover}
# Columns (fixed total N, split K cohorts x n_per subjects):
#   beta_within_rmse    - error in the population-average effect   (FALLS with K)
#   tau_rmse            - error in cross-cohort heterogeneity      (FALLS with K)
#   median_location_se  - precision for ONE location               (RISES with K)
# The crossover is where chasing the population-average estimate starts costing
# more single-site precision than it buys. Bracketed, not interpolated, because
# K is sampled on a coarse grid.
prm <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "Pooling_Sim_Output", "budget_allocation_params.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE)
NUM$panelD_N_total  <- prm$value[prm$parameter == "N_total"]
NUM$panelD_tau_true <- prm$value[prm$parameter == "tau_true"]
NUM$panelD_beta_bar <- prm$value[prm$parameter == "beta_bar"]

d  <- budget$beta_within_rmse - budget$median_location_se
i  <- which(diff(sign(d)) != 0)[1]
NUM$panelD_crossover_lo    <- budget$K[i]
NUM$panelD_crossover_hi    <- budget$K[i + 1]
NUM$panelD_crossover_n_lo  <- budget$n_per[i]
NUM$panelD_crossover_n_hi  <- budget$n_per[i + 1]

NUM$panelD_K_min <- min(budget$K); NUM$panelD_K_max <- max(budget$K)
NUM$panelD_beta_rmse_at_Kmin <- budget$beta_within_rmse[which.min(budget$K)]
NUM$panelD_beta_rmse_at_Kmax <- budget$beta_within_rmse[which.max(budget$K)]
NUM$panelD_se_at_Kmin        <- budget$median_location_se[which.min(budget$K)]
NUM$panelD_se_at_Kmax        <- budget$median_location_se[which.max(budget$K)]
NUM$panelD_beta_rmse_fold <- with(budget, beta_within_rmse[which.min(K)] /
                                          beta_within_rmse[which.max(K)])
NUM$panelD_se_fold        <- with(budget, median_location_se[which.max(K)] /
                                          median_location_se[which.min(K)])
# Does a 2-cohort design recover the true heterogeneity?
NUM$panelD_tauhat_at_Kmin <- budget$tau_hat_mean[which.min(budget$K)]
NUM$panelD_tau_bias_Kmin  <- budget$tau_hat_mean[which.min(budget$K)] - NUM$panelD_tau_true

tibble(metric = grep("^panelD", names(NUM), value = TRUE),
       value = vapply(NUM[grep("^panelD", names(NUM))],
                      function(x) format(x, digits = 4), character(1))) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

             value  = vapply(NUM, function(x) format(x, digits = 6), character(1))),

cat("exported", length(NUM), "Figure 3 numbers to Output/Hero_Numbers/\n")
